sanskrit: sarasvatīṃ tataḥ somo jagāma ṛṣiśāsanāt prabhāsaṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ sarasvatyā jagāma ha
english: Then, by the seer's command, Soma went to the Sarasvatī; he came indeed to Prabhāsa, the supreme tīrtha upon the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: amāvāsyāṃ mahātejās tatronmajjan mahādyutiḥ lokān prabhāsayām āsa śītāṃśutvam avāpa ca
english: On the new-moon day the mighty-splendored one, rising up there in great brilliance, illumined the worlds and regained his cool-rayed nature.

sanskrit: devāś ca sarve rājendra prabhāsaṃ prāpya puṣkalam somena sahitā bhūtvā dakṣasya pramukhe 'bhavan
english: And all the gods, O lord of kings, having reached abundant Prabhāsa and joined together with Soma, stood before Dakṣa.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajāpatiḥ sarvā visasarjātha devatāḥ somaṃ ca bhagavān prīto bhūyo vacanam abravīt
english: Then the Lord of Creatures dismissed all the deities, and the blessed one, pleased, spoke once more to Soma these words:

sanskrit: māvamaṃsthāḥ striyaḥ putra mā ca viprān kadā cana gaccha yuktaḥ sadā bhūtvā kuru vai śāsanaṃ mama
english: "Despise not women, my son, nor ever the brāhmaṇas. Go now, and being ever diligent, carry out my command."

sanskrit: sa visṛṣṭo mahārāja jagāmātha svam ālayam prajāś ca muditā bhūtvā bhojane ca yathā purā
english: Dismissed thus, O great king, he went to his own abode, and the creatures grew glad, partaking of nourishment as before.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathā śapto niśākaraḥ prabhāsaṃ ca yathā tīrthaṃ tīrthānāṃ pravaraṃ hy abhūt
english: All this I have told you—how the night-maker was cursed, and how Prabhāsa came to be the foremost among tīrthas.

sanskrit: amāvāsyāṃ mahārāja nityaśaḥ śaśalakṣaṇaḥ snātvā hy āpyāyate śrīmān prabhāse tīrtha uttame
english: On every new-moon day, O great king, the hare-marked one, the glorious Moon, bathing at the supreme tīrtha of Prabhāsa, is replenished.

sanskrit: ataś cainaṃ prajānanti prabhāsam iti bhūmipa prabhāṃ hi paramāṃ lebhe tasminn unmajjya candramāḥ
english: Therefore men know it as Prabhāsa, O lord of the earth; for the Moon, rising up there, attained his supreme radiance (prabhā).

sanskrit: tatas tu camasodbhedam acyutas tv agamad balī camasodbheda ity evaṃ yaṃ janāḥ kathayanty uta
english: Then the unfallen, mighty one went on to Camasodbheda—that which men speak of as Camasodbheda.

sanskrit: tatra dattvā ca dānāni viśiṣṭāni halāyudhaḥ uṣitvā rajanīm ekāṃ snātvā ca vidhivat tadā
english: There Halāyudha, having bestowed choice gifts, stayed a single night and bathed according to the prescribed rite.

sanskrit: udapānam athāgacchat tvarāvān keśavāgrajaḥ ādyaṃ svastyayanaṃ caiva tatrāvāpya mahat phalam
english: Then the elder brother of Keśava went swiftly to Udapāna, gaining there too the foremost benediction and great reward.

sanskrit: snigdhatvād oṣadhīnāṃ ca bhūmeś ca janamejaya jānanti siddhā rājendra naṣṭām api sarasvatīm
english: For by the moistness of the herbs and of the earth, O Janamejaya, the perfected ones, O lord of kings, discern the Sarasvatī even where she has vanished.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmān nadīgataṃ cāpi udapānaṃ yaśasvinaḥ tritasya ca mahārāja jagāmātha halāyudhaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: From there Halāyudha went on, O great king, to the Udapāna—the river-sunk well of the illustrious Trita.

sanskrit: tatra dattvā bahu dravyaṃ pūjayitvā tathā dvijān upaspṛśya ca tatraiva prahṛṣṭo musalāyudhaḥ
english: There the wielder of the pestle, well pleased, bestowed much wealth and honored the brāhmaṇas, and touched the water in that very place.

sanskrit: tatra dharmaparo hy āsīt tritaḥ sa sumahātapāḥ kūpe ca vasatā tena somaḥ pīto mahātmanā
english: There it was that Trita dwelt, devoted to dharma, of mighty austerity; and that great soul, while abiding in the well, drank the soma.

sanskrit: tatra cainaṃ samutsṛjya bhrātarau jagmatur gṛhān tatas tau vai śaśāpātha trito brāhmaṇasattamaḥ
english: And there, abandoning him, his two brothers went home; whereupon Trita, that best of brāhmaṇas, laid a curse upon them both.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca udapānaṃ kathaṃ brahman kathaṃ ca sumahātapāḥ patitaḥ kiṃ ca saṃtyakto bhrātṛbhyāṃ dvijasattamaḥ
english: Janamejaya said: How came the well to be, O brāhmaṇa, and how did that one of great austerity, that best of the twice-born, fall in, and why was he forsaken by his brothers?

sanskrit: kūpe kathaṃ ca hitvainaṃ bhrātarau jagmatur gṛhān etad ācakṣva me brahman yadi śrāvyaṃ hi manyase
english: And how, leaving him in the well, did the two brothers go home? Tell me this, O brāhmaṇa, if you think it fit to be heard.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca āsan pūrvayuge rājan munayo bhrātaras trayaḥ ekataś ca dvitaś caiva tritaś cādityasaṃnibhāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: In a former age, O king, there were three brother-sages, Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, resembling the sun.

sanskrit: sarve prajāpatisamāḥ prajāvantas tathaiva ca brahmalokajitaḥ sarve tapasā brahmavādinaḥ
english: All were like Prajāpati, blessed with offspring, all winners of the world of Brahman by austerity, all expounders of the Veda.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu tapasā prīto niyamena damena ca abhavad gautamo nityaṃ pitā dharmarataḥ sadā
english: Their father Gautama, ever devoted to dharma, was always pleased by their austerity, their discipline, and their self-restraint.

sanskrit: sa tu dīrgheṇa kālena teṣāṃ prītim avāpya ca jagāma bhagavān sthānam anurūpam ivātmanaḥ
english: And in the course of long time, having gained their devotion, the blessed one departed to the abode befitting himself.

sanskrit: rājānas tasya ye pūrve yājyā hy āsan mahātmanaḥ te sarve svargate tasmiṃs tasya putrān apūjayan
english: Those kings who before had been the patrons of that great soul, when he had gone to heaven, all honored his sons.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu karmaṇā rājaṃs tathaivādhyayanena ca tritaḥ sa śreṣṭhatāṃ prāpa yathaivāsya pitā tathā
english: By his works and by his study, O king, Trita attained pre-eminence, even as his father had done.

sanskrit: taṃ sma sarve mahābhāgā munayaḥ puṇyalakṣaṇāḥ apūjayan mahābhāgaṃ tathā vidvattayaiva tu
english: All the blessed sages of holy mark honored that illustrious one for his learning as well.

sanskrit: kadā cid dhi tato rājan bhrātarāv ekatadvitau yajñārthaṃ cakratuś cittaṃ dhanārthaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
english: Now once, O king, the two brothers Ekata and Dvita set their minds upon a sacrifice, and especially upon gaining wealth thereby.

sanskrit: tayoś cintā samabhavat tritaṃ gṛhya paraṃtapa yājyān sarvān upādāya pratigṛhya paśūṃs tataḥ
english: This thought arose in the two, O scorcher of foes: to take Trita with them, to gather all their patrons, and to receive cattle from them.

sanskrit: somaṃ pāsyāmahe hṛṣṭāḥ prāpya yajñaṃ mahāphalam cakruś caiva mahārāja bhrātaras traya eva ha
english: "Joyfully we shall drink the soma, having gained a sacrifice of great fruit." And so, O great king, the three brothers performed it.

sanskrit: tathā tu te parikramya yājyān sarvān paśūn prati yājayitvā tato yājyāṃl labdhvā ca subahūn paśūn
english: Going about thus among all their patrons for the sake of cattle, they performed sacrifices for them, and so obtained from those patrons very many beasts.

sanskrit: yājyena karmaṇā tena pratigṛhya vidhānataḥ prācīṃ diśaṃ mahātmāna ājagmus te maharṣayaḥ
english: Having received their due by that priestly office according to rule, those great-souled seers came toward the eastern quarter.

sanskrit: tritas teṣāṃ mahārāja purastād yāti hṛṣṭavat ekataś ca dvitaś caiva pṛṣṭhataḥ kālayan paśūn
english: Trita walked before them, O great king, gladly, while Ekata and Dvita came behind, driving the cattle.

sanskrit: tayoś cintā samabhavad dṛṣṭvā paśugaṇaṃ mahat kathaṃ na syur imā gāva āvābhyāṃ vai vinā tritam
english: Seeing the great herd of cattle, a thought arose in the two: "How might these cows be ours, the two of us, without Trita?"

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ samābhāṣya ekataś ca dvitaś ca ha yad ūcatur mithaḥ pāpau tan nibodha janeśvara
english: Conferring with one another, Ekata and Dvita—the two sinners—spoke together; hear what they said, O lord of men.

sanskrit: trito yajñeṣu kuśalas trito vedeṣu niṣṭhitaḥ anyās trito bahutarā gāvaḥ samupalapsyate
english: "Trita is skilled in sacrifices, Trita is grounded in the Vedas; Trita will obtain still other and far more numerous cows."

sanskrit: tad āvāṃ sahitau bhūtvā gāḥ prakālya vrajāvahe trito 'pi gacchatāṃ kāmam āvābhyāṃ vai vinākṛtaḥ
english: "Therefore let the two of us, joined together, drive off the cows and go; and let Trita too go where he will, parted from us."

sanskrit: teṣām āgacchatāṃ rātrau pathisthāne vṛko 'bhavat tathā kūpo 'vidūre 'bhūt sarasvatyās taṭe mahān
english: As they came on by night, a wolf appeared in their path; and not far off, on the bank of the Sarasvatī, there was a great well.

sanskrit: atha trito vṛkaṃ dṛṣṭvā pathi tiṣṭhantam agrataḥ tadbhayād apasarpan vai tasmin kūpe papāta ha agādhe sumahāghore sarvabhūtabhayaṃkare
english: Then Trita, seeing the wolf standing before him in the path, recoiled in fear of it and fell into that well—bottomless, most terrible, dreadful to all beings.

sanskrit: tritas tato mahābhāgaḥ kūpastho munisattamaḥ ārtanādaṃ tataś cakre tau tu śuśruvatur munī
english: Then the illustrious Trita, that best of sages, fallen within the well, raised a cry of distress, and the two sages heard it.

sanskrit: taṃ jñātvā patitaṃ kūpe bhrātarāv ekatadvitau vṛkatrāsāc ca lobhāc ca samutsṛjya prajagmatuḥ
english: Knowing him fallen into the well, the brothers Ekata and Dvita, out of fear of the wolf and out of greed, abandoned him and went on.

sanskrit: bhrātṛbhyāṃ paśulubdhābhyām utsṛṣṭaḥ sa mahātapāḥ udapāne mahārāja nirjale pāṃsusaṃvṛte
english: Forsaken by his two brothers, greedy for cattle, that one of great austerity lay, O great king, in the well, waterless and choked with dust.

sanskrit: trita ātmānam ālakṣya kūpe vīruttṛṇāvṛte nimagnaṃ bharataśreṣṭha pāpakṛn narake yathā
english: Trita beheld himself sunk in the well overgrown with creepers and grass, O best of Bhāratas, as a sinner sunk in hell.

sanskrit: buddhyā hy agaṇayat prājño mṛtyor bhīto hy asomapaḥ somaḥ kathaṃ nu pātavya ihasthena mayā bhavet
english: Wise as he was, fearing death and yet undrinker of soma, he reckoned in his mind: "How might the soma be drunk by me, while I bide here?"

sanskrit: sa evam anusaṃcintya tasmin kūpe mahātapāḥ dadarśa vīrudhaṃ tatra lambamānāṃ yadṛcchayā
english: Pondering thus in that well, the one of great austerity saw a creeper hanging there by chance.

sanskrit: pāṃsugraste tataḥ kūpe vicintya salilaṃ muniḥ agnīn saṃkalpayām āsa hotre cātmānam eva ca
english: Then in that dust-clogged well the sage, imagining the water, conceived the sacrificial fires, and himself as the hotṛ-priest.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ vīrudhaṃ somaṃ saṃkalpya sumahātapāḥ ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni manasā cintayan muniḥ grāvāṇaḥ śarkarāḥ kṛtvā pracakre 'bhiṣavaṃ nṛpa
english: Then, conceiving that creeper to be the soma, the sage of mighty austerity, calling to mind in thought the Ṛcs, the Yajuses, and the Sāmans, and making the pebbles into the pressing-stones, performed the pressing, O king.

sanskrit: ājyaṃ ca salilaṃ cakre bhāgāṃś ca tridivaukasām somasyābhiṣavaṃ kṛtvā cakāra tumulaṃ dhvanim
english: He made the water into clarified butter and the portions for the dwellers of the threefold heaven; and having pressed the soma, he raised a tumultuous sound.

sanskrit: sa cāviśad divaṃ rājan svaraḥ śaikṣas tritasya vai samavāpa ca taṃ yajñaṃ yathoktaṃ brahmavādibhiḥ
english: And that trained, well-pitched chant of Trita pierced heaven, O king; and he accomplished that sacrifice as it is prescribed by the expounders of the Veda.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā yajñe tritasya sumahātmanaḥ āvignaṃ tridivaṃ sarvaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca na budhyate
english: As the sacrifice of the great-souled Trita went forward, all the threefold heaven was thrown into agitation, and none could fathom the cause.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutumulaṃ śabdaṃ śuśrāvātha bṛhaspatiḥ śrutvā caivābravīd devān sarvān devapurohitaḥ
english: Then Bṛhaspati heard that most tumultuous sound, and hearing it, the chaplain of the gods spoke to all the deities:

sanskrit: tritasya vartate yajñas tatra gacchāmahe surāḥ sa hi kruddhaḥ sṛjed anyān devān api mahātapāḥ
english: "The sacrifice of Trita is in progress; let us go thither, O gods. For that one of great austerity, if angered, might create other gods as well."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya sahitāḥ sarvadevatāḥ prayayus tatra yatrāsau tritayajñaḥ pravartate
english: Hearing that word of his, all the deities together set forth to the place where that sacrifice of Trita was being performed.

sanskrit: te tatra gatvā vibudhās taṃ kūpaṃ yatra sa tritaḥ dadṛśus taṃ mahātmānaṃ dīkṣitaṃ yajñakarmasu
english: The gods, having gone there to the well where Trita was, beheld that great soul consecrated for the sacrificial rites.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā cainaṃ mahātmānaṃ śriyā paramayā yutam ūcuś cātha mahābhāgaṃ prāptā bhāgārthino vayam
english: And seeing that great soul endowed with surpassing splendor, they said to the illustrious one: "We have come, seeking our portions."

sanskrit: athābravīd ṛṣir devān paśyadhvaṃ māṃ divaukasaḥ asmin pratibhaye kūpe nimagnaṃ naṣṭacetasam
english: Then the seer said to the gods: "Behold me, O dwellers of heaven, sunk in this fearful well and well-nigh out of my senses."

sanskrit: tatas trito mahārāja bhāgāṃs teṣāṃ yathāvidhi mantrayuktān samadadāt te ca prītās tadābhavan
english: Then Trita, O great king, gave them their portions according to rule, accompanied by the sacred formulas; and they were well pleased thereat.

sanskrit: tato yathāvidhi prāptān bhāgān prāpya divaukasaḥ prītātmāno dadus tasmai varān yān manasecchati
english: Then the dwellers of heaven, having received the portions duly obtained, glad at heart, granted him the boons that he desired in his mind.

sanskrit: sa tu vavre varaṃ devāṃs trātum arhatha mām itaḥ yaś cehopaspṛśet kūpe sa somapagatiṃ labhet
english: And he chose this boon: "You ought to deliver me from here; and whoever touches the water in this well, let him attain the state of the soma-drinkers."

sanskrit: tatra cormimatī rājann utpapāta sarasvatī tayotkṣiptas tritas tasthau pūjayaṃs tridivaukasaḥ
english: Thereupon, O king, the Sarasvatī surged up there full of waves, and Trita, lifted by her, stood honoring the dwellers of heaven.

sanskrit: tatheti coktvā vibudhā jagmū rājan yathāgatam tritaś cāpy agamat prītaḥ svam eva nilayaṃ tadā
english: Saying "So be it," the gods went, O king, as they had come; and Trita too, well pleased, then went to his own abode.

sanskrit: kruddhaḥ sa tu samāsādya tāv ṛṣī bhrātarau tadā uvāca paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ śaśāpa ca mahātapāḥ
english: But that one of great austerity, having reached his two brother-sages, then in anger spoke harsh words to them and cursed them:

sanskrit: paśulubdhau yuvāṃ yasmān mām utsṛjya pradhāvitau tasmād rūpeṇa teṣāṃ vai daṃṣṭriṇām abhitaś carau
english: "Since the two of you, greedy for cattle, forsook me and ran away, therefore in the form of fanged beasts you shall roam about,

sanskrit: bhavitārau mayā śaptau pāpenānena karmaṇā prasavaś caiva yuvayor golāṅgūlarkṣavānarāḥ
english: cursed by me for this evil deed; and your offspring shall be langurs, bears, and monkeys."

sanskrit: ity ukte tu tadā tena kṣaṇād eva viśāṃ pate tathābhūtāv adṛśyetāṃ vacanāt satyavādinaḥ
english: And when this was spoken by him, that very instant, O lord of peoples, the two were seen so transformed by the word of the truth-speaker.

sanskrit: tatrāpy amitavikrāntaḥ spṛṣṭvā toyaṃ halāyudhaḥ dattvā ca vividhān dāyān pūjayitvā ca vai dvijān
english: There too Halāyudha of boundless valor touched the water, bestowed gifts of many kinds, and honored the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: udapānaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ nadīgatam adīnātmā prāpto vinaśanaṃ tadā
english: And having seen that river-sunk well and praised it again and again, the undaunted one then reached Vinaśana.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vinaśanaṃ rājann ājagāma halāyudhaḥ śūdrābhīrān prati dveṣād yatra naṣṭā sarasvatī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O king, Halāyudha came to Vinaśana, where the Sarasvatī vanished out of loathing for the Śūdras and the Ābhīras.

sanskrit: yasmāt sā bharataśreṣṭha dveṣān naṣṭā sarasvatī tasmāt tad ṛṣayo nityaṃ prāhur vinaśaneti ha
english: Because she, the Sarasvatī, O best of Bhāratas, vanished out of loathing, therefore the seers ever call that place Vinaśana.

sanskrit: tac cāpy upaspṛśya balaḥ sarasvatyāṃ mahābalaḥ subhūmikaṃ tato 'gacchat sarasvatyās taṭe vare
english: And there too Bala of mighty strength touched the waters of the Sarasvatī, and then went on to Subhūmika upon the fair bank of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: tatra cāpsarasaḥ śubhrā nityakālam atandritāḥ krīḍābhir vimalābhiś ca krīḍanti vimalānanāḥ
english: There the radiant apsarases, ever unwearied, of unblemished countenance, sport at all times with pure and lovely games.

sanskrit: tatra devāḥ sagandharvā māsi māsi janeśvara abhigacchanti tat tīrthaṃ puṇyaṃ brāhmaṇasevitam
english: There, O lord of men, the gods together with the gandharvas come month after month to that holy tīrtha frequented by brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tatrādṛśyanta gandharvās tathaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ sametya sahitā rājan yathāprāptaṃ yathāsukham
english: There the gandharvas and likewise the throngs of apsarases were seen, gathered and joined together, O king, each as it chanced and at their ease.

sanskrit: tatra modanti devāś ca pitaraś ca savīrudhaḥ puṇyaiḥ puṣpaiḥ sadā divyaiḥ kīryamāṇāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: There the gods and the ancestors rejoice amid the herbs, ever showered again and again with holy, heavenly blossoms.

sanskrit: ākrīḍabhūmiḥ sā rājaṃs tāsām apsarasāṃ śubhā subhūmiketi vikhyātā sarasvatyās taṭe vare
english: That fair playground of those apsarases, O king, is renowned as Subhūmika, upon the lovely bank of the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: tatra snātvā ca dattvā ca vasu vipreṣu mādhavaḥ śrutvā gītaṃ ca tad divyaṃ vāditrāṇāṃ ca niḥsvanam
english: There the Mādhava, having bathed and bestowed wealth upon the brāhmaṇas, and having heard that heavenly song and the sound of the instruments—

sanskrit: chāyāś ca vipulā dṛṣṭvā devagandharvarakṣasām gandharvāṇāṃ tatas tīrtham āgacchad rohiṇīsutaḥ
english: and having seen the broad shadows of the gods, gandharvas, and rākṣasas—the son of Rohiṇī then came to the tīrtha of the gandharvas.

sanskrit: viśvāvasumukhās tatra gandharvās tapasānvitāḥ nṛttavāditragītaṃ ca kurvanti sumanoramam
english: There the gandharvas led by Viśvāvasu, endowed with austerity, make most delightful dance, music, and song.

sanskrit: tatra dattvā haladharo viprebhyo vividhaṃ vasu ajāvikaṃ gokharoṣṭraṃ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā
english: There the plough-bearer bestowed upon the brāhmaṇas manifold wealth—goats and sheep, cattle, asses and camels, gold and silver as well—

sanskrit: bhojayitvā dvijān kāmaiḥ saṃtarpya ca mahādhanaiḥ prayayau sahito vipraiḥ stūyamānaś ca mādhavaḥ
english: and having fed the twice-born with all they desired and gratified them with great riches, the Mādhava went onward in the company of the brāhmaṇas, being praised by them.

sanskrit: tasmād gandharvatīrthāc ca mahābāhur ariṃdamaḥ gargasroto mahātīrtham ājagāmaikakuṇḍalī
english: And from that gandharva-tīrtha the mighty-armed subduer of foes, wearing a single earring, came to the great tīrtha of Gargasrotas.
